answer: Each epoch every identity must pass two birds before the horizon: a falcon re-derives its fresh task live in sixty seconds, and a raven, a randomly drawn peer, audits one past task from its public history. Only work finished before the epoch's horizon counts toward weight, so a fake cannot backfill a history after the fact. An honest agent does one task per epoch and passes both birds cheaply. An attacker with a thousand fakes must produce a thousand live solutions inside sixty seconds and keep a thousand histories consistent for the raven, so the flood's cost rises linearly with every fake.
